status.deprecated:
The season is the source of a chapter's visibility: `Season.sequence[].status`, per locale. The creator
mirrors the season status here on save, only for older viewer builds; nothing reads it any more.

keyvisual.description: a plain string = the image path (older chapters, e.g. catpope 3–5; the viewer reads both)

featuring.description: Who appears in this chapter: registry character ids, a subset of the season's cast (`cast:<toon>`), in display order. Optional and editorial – suggested from the chapter's VN scenes (`chapterSceneCharacters`), set by hand for plain scroll chapters. The reader shows it on the chapter list item and at the chapter start.

related_items.description: Items that go with this chapter (catalog item ids, in order; language-neutral – the creator writes the same list to every locale), agents/ITEMS.md "Players, albums, related items". Stored + edited; the reader does not show it yet.

highlight.description: how "Show hints" highlights the chapter's tap / hover / sound areas (fx.ts `HIGHLIGHTERS`); none = fireflies

Language.description: Content languages (a toon's `languages`); ISO 639-1. Korean is `ko` (2026-10-02, was the unused country code `kr`).

AudioTrack.description: A music track or a sample-library sound. `path` = the default file (the medium level, 128k – what older readers and a reader without a known level play); `variants` = one file per quality level (low 96k / medium 128k / high 320k, PLAN.md "RULE: one file per quality level"), toon-relative like `path`. A missing level falls back to the next lower one.

QualityVariants.description: One file per quality level (CDN paths like `src`); a missing level falls back (`pickQualityVariant`).

continues.description: Linked groups (owner 2026-10-06): this group flows straight into the next group on the same page, no follow-up bar between. A chain = consecutive groups where every one but the last continues (`chainOf` in chains.ts). Any group may have a VN script or slice events (their scripts run one after another on the page); after a group whose script can jump away, the next group needs a label.

end.description: Where the reader goes when this group – the chain's last – is done, instead of the next group / chapter. Ignored on a group that `continues`.

endless.description: Endless (owner 2026-10-15, FEATURES 10.100 §8): a horizontal group as an inline, screen-high band the reader drags sideways with momentum; it loops without end (no clones). Without it a horizontal group is the pinned strip.

RendererParams.description: A horizontal group's params (closed: the schema refuses any other key). Without `endless` a horizontal group is the pinned strip (owner 2026-10-06): it leaves the reading column, its slices side by side at the screen's full height; scrolling down pins it and moves it sideways (1:1, no snapping), then reading goes on downwards; on a desktop it can go full screen (← →). `groupLayout` / `rendererOf` (flow.ts) name the three layouts.

sensitive.description: hidden while "Hide sensitive content" is on (members: on by default, guests: always on)

image.description: CDN path of the slice image (1x WebP, 390 px wide) relative to the toon's folder; the poster of a video slice

width.description: Size of the image in px (1x): the reader reserves the space before the lazy image loads.

imageVariants.description: The image per quality level (owner 2026-10-03, PLAN.md "Slices"): low = 1x (= `image`), medium = 2x, high = 3x (390 / 780 / 1170 px wide WebP, `<name>.2x.webp`). The reader picks by its media quality (`pickQualityVariant`); none = just `image`.

items.description: catalog items placed on the slice, drawn above the image; with the text boxes ONE layer stack (`layer` on each entry, `sliceLayers`) – without any `layer` below the text boxes

Slice.description: One slice. `sensitive: true` (SensitiveFlag, the same in every language) = while the reader's "Hide sensitive content" is on, the image / video is blurred, the slice's sounds stay silent and a small note sits on it (agents/ITEMS.md "Sensitive slices").

src.description: CDN path of an H.264 MP4, relative to the toon's folder like `image`: the default file – it plays when no variant fits the reader's quality (`pickQualityVariant`) and in readers that don't know `variants`.

variants.description: One file per quality level (media-quality.ts): low = 480p, medium = 720p, high = 1080p. The reader takes its quality setting's level, else the nearest lower one, else `src`. No adaptive streaming (HLS) – one file per load.

autoplay.description: default true: plays while the slice is in view (paused outside, poster only with reduced motion; ignored with `player`)

player.description: A video player instead of the loop: sound, native controls (fullscreen through them), started by the reader, no loop. The slice's `width` / `height` are the video's aspect ratio at the slice width (no 390 × 625 crop). While it plays the chapter's music is paused; watching it to its end (≥ 95 %) is the slice's reading progress.

controls.description: the browser's basic controls (play/pause, time, volume, fullscreen); default: on for a player, off for a loop

viewport.description: fills the viewport instead of the reading column, placed like this (`SliceViewport`); omitted = in the column

frame.description: in the column: the box's ratio + how the video sits in it (`SliceFrame`); omitted = "Original" (the media's ratio)

SliceVideo.description: A video instead of the slice image. The slice's `image` is its poster. By default a muted, inline loop that plays while in view; with `player` a video to watch (a music video, a trailer).

ratio.description: "w:h" (a preset like "9:16", or any) or [w, h]; between 4:1 and 1:4

SliceFrame.description: The box of a video slice in the reading column (`SliceVideo.frame`, owner 2026-10-01): a ratio instead of the media's own ("Original" = no `frame`). The slice is 390 px wide and `width` / `height` follow the ratio (390 × 693 for 9:16), so the reader reserves the space before anything loads; the media is placed in the box with `fit` / `position` like a full-viewport video (`SliceViewport`). Doesn't apply in full viewport (the box is the viewport there).

layer.description: a click / hover area's place in the slice's ONE layer stack (`VNSliceEvent.layer`, layers.ts – BACKLOG 10.54)

rect.description: hit area in % of the slice; none = the whole slice

gate.description: only play if not already playing (default false)

id.description: Stable key (Figma node id) → i18n file.

rect.description: % of the slice box: x / y = the position of the `anchor` point (none = the top-left corner). `height` optional (needed for `valign` and auto-fit).

text.description: Array entries are rendered as separate lines / paragraphs; `\n` inside an entry is a line break.

frame.description: caption / narration / lyrics: draw the paper box + ink border, default true (false = bare text, use `mask`). bubble: draw a speech bubble (paper, ink outline, a tail), default false – the bubble shape of chapter 1/2 art is in the image; the creator sets `true` for new bubbles on text-free art.

shape.description: a drawn bubble's outline (bubble with `frame: true`), default 'box' ('oval' = older data, drawn as a box)

tail.description: a drawn bubble's tail (bubble with `frame: true`), default 'bottom-left' for a box, 'none' for a wobbly one

size.description: Font size in % of the slice width (rendered as cqw). Default 4.

font.description: Default 'lettering' for bubble, 'mono' for caption/narration (matches chapter 1).

anchor.description: The point of the box that `rect.x` / `rect.y` place (anchor.ts): the box grows away from it when its drawn size differs from the stored one. Default 'tl' (top-left).

stroke.description: Outline of the letters (a CSS colour), e.g. white letters with an ink outline for an onomatopoeia; none = no outline.

strokeWidth.description: outline width in em of the font size, default 0.14

letterSpacing.description: letter spacing in em of the font size (owner 2026-10-03), e.g. 0.05; default the font's own (0)

lineHeight.description: line height as a multiple of the font size (owner 2026-10-17); default the font's own: lettering 1.1, mono 1.35

scale.description: Uniform scale of the whole box (frame, text, mask) around its centre, after `rect` and `size` are laid out. Default 1. Lets an onomatopoeia grow or shrink without re-wrapping its text.

mask.description: Fill rect (+ pad) before drawing the text, to cover text baked into legacy art. true = '#ffffff'.
mask.deprecated: owner 2026-10-03: the chapter's art is re-imported text-free; the dialog data stays. Still drawn for old data.

pad.description: Extra mask padding in % of slice width. Default 0.5.

layer.description: Place in the slice's ONE layer stack of text boxes, placed items and click / hover areas (`SliceItem.layer`, layers.ts): higher = drawn on top. None = the old order (sample areas, items, text boxes, event areas) – see `sliceLayers`.

Dialog.description: A live, translatable text box on top of a slice image (see agents/DESIGN.md → Part 2).

DialogVariant.description: An onomatopoeia is a text box too (the "onomatopoeia" text preset: white letters with an ink outline); a `showTextBox` event reveals any text box with an effect (`VNShowTextBoxEvent` `params.dialog`). `lyrics` = a song line (owner 2026-10-17): the caption box with musical notes on its border, drawn by the reader outside the text flow.

id.description: stable key of this placement (pickups are remembered by it); `<item>-<n>`

rect.description: % of the slice box: x / y = the `anchor` point (none = top-left); `height` omitted = the icon's own ratio

events.description: events: run on tap (no trigger – the tap is the trigger)

repeat.description: events: how often a tap runs them (recurrence.ts, like a slice trigger's `repeat`); none = every tap

respawn.description: pickup: when it is back after being taken (respawn.ts). None = the item's default (catalog `respawn`; an item without one never reappears); `never` = once here even if the item could reappear; an interval = an override within the item's range (every visit, every n minutes / hours / days). Once per period; the catalog's limits still apply.

sound.description: pickup: the sound when it lands in the bag (agents/FX.md) – none = the item's (catalog `sound`), else "pling"; `none` = silent

variant.description: pickup: one of the item's variants (its icon here, the variant goes into the inventory); none = the item itself

variable.description: `toon` scope: the story variable the answer goes to

placeholder.description: a hint in the empty input line

maxLength.description: at most this many characters (default 24, at most 200)

answer.description: a ready answer as a button under the input line: its text (none = no button)

default.description: what the answer button (or an empty answer) stores; none = nothing is stored – the variable stays unset, so a later condition can tell it apart

VNEventCondition.description: an event's `if`: the simple test (the creator's default) or an expression

VNConditionOp.description: "Only if" on any event (owner 2026-10-03): the event runs only when the reader's variable passes the test, else it is skipped. Numbers compare as numbers; `set` / `unset` ask whether the variable has a value at all.

VNExprCondition.description: "Only if" as an expression (agents/EXPRESSIONS.md §3, the advanced form): ink's logic on the expression engine and the reader's resolver – `count("s1c2-e4k2j9x1") < 3 and not has("cucumber")`. A syntax error can't be saved.

VNAction.description: what a choice does when picked – one action or several in order (e.g. add 15 minutes, then jump)

item.description: a catalog item id (picked from the catalog – a script can't make items)

variant.description: one of the item's variants (a colour of the sunglasses); none = the item itself

VNGiveItem.description: give the reader a catalog item (BACKLOG 10.38: an item is never a story variable) – the inventory's rules apply: the item must be grantable from the story, its max count, once per place (a replay grants nothing)

VNTakeItem.description: take a catalog item from the reader (owner 2026-10-07, BACKLOG 10.38): only an item the catalog marks `takeable` (never a physical one); all or nothing – with too few nothing is taken (and in a choice's list the actions after it don't run: a trade never gives for free); the story goes on. `repeat`: how often it takes again (the trigger intervals; none = every time).

TimedInterval.description: A timed interval: every n minutes / hours / days (n a whole number ≥ 1, at most a year).

toon.description: `type: 'chapter'` only: the chapter (and `label` / `anyOf`) of ANOTHER toon (owner 2026-10-06, "at label"); absent = this toon. `type: 'toon'` stays the toon's page. Variables travel along (one save game); their names have a domain (variables.ts: `x` is the toon's own, `global.x` every toon's, `toptoy.x` toptoy's).

anyOf.description: a random group of this chapter instead of `label` (owner 2026-10-03, the chapter 2 stroll): one of these labels, never the group the reader is on (`pickJumpLabel`)

VNDivert.description: continue the group's script at a named point (`label` event) – the story's own branch, no page change

look.description: a look of the persona (e.g. `helmet`); none = its default look

VNCharacterRef.description: A character reference in a VN event (joinScene / leaveScene), as authored: `{ character, persona, look?, mood?, variant? }` (`variant` = the view). The old form `{ name, position: { variant } }` and old character ids (plf, cat, mountain-tiger → catpope personas) still resolve (`normalizeSceneRef` in characters.ts). The same character may be in a scene with several personas (Cat Pope meets Cat Pope · Biker).

CharacterView.description: A view (framing) of a character in a scene.

delay.description: ms before the box appears, default 0 (max 5000)

mode.description: `mono` = one at a time (queued), `poly` = together; default poly

wait.description: the script waits for a tap before it continues

stay.description: after its effect the box stays (default true) or disappears again (`false`, after `delay` + `duration`)

sound.description: the sound when it appears (agents/FX.md): none = the effect's own (pop, slam, fade, typeOn have one), `none` = silent

shake.description: slam: what shakes when it lands – none set = its slice, `screen` = the whole screen, `none` = nothing (owner 2026-10-08)

ShowTextBoxParams.description: A text box revealed by this event (owner 2026-10-03, option B; any text box, e.g. an onomatopoeia): `dialog` is the id of a text box (`Dialog.id`) on the event's slice, or for a group script on one of the group's slices. The box stays hidden until the event fires, then appears with `effect` / `delay` / `duration` and stays; the box gives the look (variant, font, colour, outline, rotation, scale, text per language), the event the timing.

FxSoundChoice.description: a sound choice in content: one of the sounds, or `none` (none set = the effect's own)

target.description: `slice` (default) = the slice in view (a slice's own event: that slice), `screen` = the whole screen

duration.description: ms (default per effect: shake 450, flash 420, punch 380, vignette 1600; at most 3000)

sound.description: none = the effect's own sound (boom, zap, thud, hum), `none` = silent

wait.description: the script waits until it is over

FxParams.description: An impact (agents/FX.md): the slice shakes, flashes white, zooms in and out quickly, or dark edges close in – with its sound. Everything stays inside the visible screen: nothing scrolls or jumps.

map.description: how the map shows it (owner 2026-10-11: "im Creator auswählen können, wie die Karte aufgeht"): `open` = the map opens and plays the reveal, also when scrolled into; `toast` = the toast only (a tap on it shows the reveal); unset = by the trigger (a script / a tap opens it, scrolling and hovering show the toast)

UnlockLocationParams.description: A place of the world map is discovered (agents/MAP.md §3.1, §8.5a): `places[id].unlocked` in the reader's save game – a set operation (again = nothing). The reader sees a toast "<place> unlocked"; in a VN script, a click trigger or an item tap the map opens, flies to the place, shows it and closes again (not on an intersect / hover trigger – scrolling is not hijacked – unless `map` says `open`). `silent`: the state only (no toast, no map). A tap on the toast, or on the new place in the map, plays the reveal any time.

who.description: a character id (registry); missing = the reader's own avatar

MigrateParams.description: A move to another region of the world map (agents/MAP.md §8.10, owner 2026-10-12: "migration is the action that facilitates this – it is an event"): the reader's avatar (no `who`) or a character is registered there (the save game's `map.residences`); then the welcome plays – the region's sign, its representative in portrait saying the region's greeting, or the narrator when none is elected. The script waits until the welcome is closed. `silent`: the registration only.

SetAvatarLocationParams.description: The reader is here now (owner 2026-10-15: "the avatar should go where ever the reader last went, so reading also moves the avatar"): the reader's own avatar stands at the place (the save game's `map.avatar`, research/CAVE.md D1) – the map's walking starts from there. No toast. A place the reader can't see yet (hidden, not unlocked) or not on the map: nothing happens – put an `unlockLocation` before it.

SliceItemRespawn.description: A placement's choice: `never` = once even if the item could reappear; none = the item's default

RecurrenceInterval.description: Every page view (`visit`: a new page or a reload starts a new one), or every n minutes / hours / days.

variable.description: `toon` scope: the story variable the answer goes to

placeholder.description: a hint in the empty input line

maxLength.description: at most this many characters (default 24, at most 200)

answer.description: a ready answer as a button under the input line: its text (none = no button)

default.description: what the answer button (or an empty answer) stores; none = nothing is stored – the variable stays unset, so a later condition can tell it apart

repeat.description: how often the trigger runs its events (recurrence.ts): none = every time; once per page view, once for good (the save game), once per n minutes / hours / days. Events with the same trigger run as one.

RefLink.description: A group stored on its own (a scene): `src` = `chapter<N>/<name>.json` (EntityKey::sceneOfRef); id / type are unused leftovers

GroupEnd.description: A group's authored end (`Group.end`): the destination; `auto` = go there at once, else the follow-up bar offers it
